| [DR-1092](DR-1092-the-road-signs-its-own-answer.md) | **The road signs its own answer — eight days of outage that never happened, because a content type was read as a verdict.** #2057 ran from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-17 with 38 comments, every one a bot, every one the same headline: NO PAGES FUNCTION IS RUNNING, EVERY NAS-backed road is dark at once, Cloudflare-side, no code change in this repository reaches it. **It is false, measured 2026-10-17 — and the probe cannot tell a working road from a dark one at all, so every reading it gave for eight days is unreliable.** Said precisely: NOT proven is that the 2026-10-09 lockout never happened — Darrell and Christina really were locked out and really photographed `Unexpected end of JSON input`, and that night may have had a genuine cause. This measurement cannot say, because the instrument was incapable of telling the two apart. The alarm has been UNINFORMATIVE since 2026-10-09, not provably false on the first night; claiming otherwise would be the over-claim DR-0076 forbids, in a record whose whole subject is an unmeasured claim. On it a zone Worker was written to route around a fault that did not exist (DR-1068), the absolute Funnel origin went back into the client bundle with its written cross-origin hazard, and eight days of real faults sat under an hourly alarm that was always wrong (P53). THE CAUSE: the verdict was the CONTENT TYPE of `/automation-status`, where text/html was taken to mean the SPA shell answered. But `/automation-status` is a PROXY, three lines over `makeFunnelProxy`, and a proxy returns the upstream's body AND the upstream's content type; it is not one of the Funnel's mounts, so it lands on the Funnel root and comes back as the NAS's own HTML page. The Function ran perfectly and returned HTML, and one road was generalized to a whole layer in a sentence nobody ever measured. THE PROBE PRINTED THE DISPROOF ON ITS OWN LINE EVERY RUN FOR EIGHT DAYS and nobody compared them: `/automation-status` is `<!DOCTYPE html>`, tab-indented, carrying `X-UA-Compatible`; `app/dist/index.html` is `<!doctype html>`, space-indented, with ZERO occurrences of X-UA-Compatible. Two different documents, side by side in the same log. EVERYTHING ELSE MEASURED AND CLEAN: wrangler 3.90.0 (not v4), `Compiled Worker successfully` + `Uploading Functions bundle`, `dist/_routes.json` carrying `/automation-status` and `/sb/*`, no catch-all in `_redirects`, the Pages project holding poetech.us with every deployment `deploy -> success`, and the Funnel answering 11 direct calls healthy (200 in 0.30 s; keyless RPC 401 in ~0.18 s; a burst of eight in parallel all 401, allow-origin *) — no throttle. And site-health's OWN /sb checks, including a real sign-in POST with a body, PASSED in the same minute the headline fired: the ledger's evidence contradicted the ledger's headline and nothing read them together. THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A BETTER GUESS: a content type can never answer "did a Function run", because a proxy's whole job is to hand back somebody else's content type. Every road now SIGNS its answer `x-poetech-road: pages-function` on all three return paths (proxied, unreachable-502, HTML-5xx-502); only code at the edge can set a response header, a static fallback sets none, so the signature's ABSENCE is the dark road for any content type and any status. Additive — upstream headers copied first and never dropped. The witnesses now READ it: site-health decides on the signature and prints the content type as a note, and on /sb the two split cleanly (unsigned = the transport gone, the 2026-10-09 lockout; signed BUT html = the NAS answering a page where JSON belongs, a real fault with a different owner), because naming the wrong layer is what cost eight days. ONE ROAD IS NEVER A LAYER: cf-pages-diagnose now probes five roads across both hosts and prints a tally, so MIXED, ALL DARK and ALL LIT can never again look the same. 9 cases weighted at the shape that fooled everybody (a proxied text/html answer must carry the signature); proven to catch three ways — the success path stops signing (3 fail), the unreachable-502 stops signing (1 fail), site-health reverts to content-type (1 fail) — each restored BYTE-IDENTICAL by `cmp` and green after. A FOURTH MUTATION PROVED NOTHING AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: its anchor no longer existed so the file was never changed and the suite passed — DR-1080's "mutation that does not mutate", hit again the same week; every mutation now asserts its anchor first, and restoration is checked with `cmp`, never `git diff --stat`, which cannot tell a restored file from an edited one while the real edits are uncommitted. The witnesses are asserted to CONSUME the header so factory and instrument cannot drift apart silently, and the retired false headline is asserted ABSENT. `decision-citation-guard` caught this record missing before it was written. NOT DONE, named rather than implied: the 00:11 UTC 502 on /sb is unexplained and not reproducible (11 direct calls healthy) — a 502 there is our own proxy's JSON, so the Function RAN and the Funnel blipped, `re-review: 2026-10-20`; DR-1068's Worker is NOT deployed and the token cannot deploy it anyway (measured: zones 0, scripts 0, Pages-only), `re-review: 2026-10-24`; the 2026-10-09 client-bundle unlock is NOT reverted though it now could be, `re-review: 2026-10-20`; #2057 is NOT closed, only corrected by a comment carrying this measurement; and `functions/api/*`, /geocode, /link and /store/apk carry their own logic and stay unsigned, `re-review: 2026-10-24`. Both workflows parse; lint clean; gates green by exit code. | accepted | B | the live-site witness; the same-origin roads; #2057 | VERIFICATION-DOCTRINE, PERPETUAL-IMPROVEMENT, HOLD-THE-HAND-OF-THE-PROCESS, DO-THE-WORK |

Ways and documentation": "Add this process to your and our Ways and documentation for making sure we do it every time." The conformance sibling of Reality-Trace (DR-0061): Reality-Trace checks a surface against real *data* before building; this checks a built process against its documented *intent* so the two never drift. Four steps, run out loud without being re-asked, before "done"/"works" or whenever asked if it works: (1) SHOULD — cite the documented intent, and if it's undocumented, writing the spec is the first gap; (2) ARE — trace the real code path end-to-end + observe running behavior, honest about what only a live session confirms; (3) GAPS — name every divergence plainly, never soften a miss; (4) CLOSE — ship a fix OR record a why + `re-review:` date (DR-0075), never a silent drop. Plain quotation marks are deliberately NOT stripped — that would open a trivial evasion (wrap a real ask in quotes and pass), and a guard that can be talked past is not a guard; the measured proof is that the original plain-quoted reply STILL flags after the change. Cost is a writing discipline (pattern names go in backticks), not a loophole. Proven with 30 tests including an explicit EVASION GUARD case. Honest limit recorded: this fixes precision, not intent — the guard stays blunt on purpose, since blunt-and-unevadable beats clever-and-permeable | accepted | A | the live reply path | VERIFICATION-DOCTRINE, GOVERN-EXECUTE-ADVISE, PERPETUAL-IMPROVEMENT, DECISION-RECORDS |

DR-0108's "a stated *can't* is an unverified premise" gains its binding inverse: **a stated *you can* is a premise too.** And "purge it for me" is measurably unavailable — the Gmail connector has **no delete verb**, Drive none, there is **no Photos connector at all**, and Takeout has no API. Decides: absent reads as absent (onTime/late are NULL not 0 without a due day — a fabricated "0 late" on a credit record is worse than a blank); parseStatementSummary reads the header block (balance, minimum, PAYMENT DUE DATE, APR) with every field independently optional; the issuer's statement balance WINS and the drift is reported since a drift is usually a missing import; payoffWith REFUSES when the payment is below the monthly interest, and bestPlays ranks that alarm above any rate optimisation; DebtStatementUpload reuses the proven pipeline rather than a second importer; provisionFromStatement creates the account+vendor for an unseen card and REUSES an existing one (a duplicate splits a card's history in two); bank-formats fingerprints on the HEADER not the filename and its load-bearing case is `changed` — a stale column map would shift every field by one and import a year of wrong numbers confidently; nothing is written until Import is pressed. | [DR-0303](DR-0303-the-list-never-carries-the-bytes-and-the-backend-needs-its-own-witness.md) | **Everyone was locked out of every app on an egress quota — the list never carries the bytes, and the backend needs a witness of its own.** Darrell 2026-08-13: *"Everyone got logged out of their accounts and their pins aren't working to get them back in… Christina and Shay my sister's MooreDivahs App and my wife's TLC Therapy Solutions App… also I'm no longer logged into PoeTech App"*, then *"you go to supabase and check."* **poetech.us was UP the whole time** — Cloudflare served the shell, the deploy ledger was green, site-health had nothing to report. The real spend is `public.feedback`: **119 rows, 6.4 MB, of which 6.2 MB is base64 image data carried by 24 rows** (largest single value 425 kB) — and `subscribeFeedback` pulled all of it with `.select('*')`, no limit, once per SIGN-IN for EVERY signed-in user (wired into the main app shell, not an admin surface) and again in full on every realtime INSERT by anyone. The money decision is Darrell's alone and the agent spent nothing. **Two defects in this record's own SQL were caught by RUNNING it against a temp table with seven row shapes, not reading it:** `false OR NULL` is NULL, so `has_screenshot` returned NULL — not false — for the 95-of-119 empty case, where the client's fallback would have computed the right answer for the wrong reason (*"nothing should happen by luck"*); and an EMPTY `screenshots` array shadowed a legacy `screenshot`, so the two columns disagreed about the same row. **The structural finding outlives the fix:** every instrument was green because not one makes an authenticated request to the backend — a 402 moves none of them, since the HTML still serves. Closed here: site-health step 7 probes `auth/v1/health` with the anon key (the path the app walks), files 402 on the incident ledger naming the violation, retries once before calling it unreachable, and NEVER reads unmeasured as healthy. | [DR-0328](DR-0328-a-frozen-tab-must-not-cost-every-read-five-seconds.md) | **A frozen tab must not cost every read five seconds — the acquire window fits inside the read budget, and the fourth bound was the signal.** Hours after the morning's outage was fixed, on the just-deployed build 3822a4e, Darrell's Properties card showed **four identical `not-reached` lines** while the NAS was MEASURED healthy (`supabase-auth` healthy; `supabase-rest` connected to PostgreSQL 15.8 with its schema cache loaded 13:15:14; the database returning transactions=3088, study_entries=45; RLS proofs passing) — and then one line from him settled it: *"it worked in incognito."* Isolated storage, no sibling poetech.us tab. `not-reached` is `boundedRead`'s TIMEOUT fallback, never something the database said, so the requests were not being answered from HIS BROWSER: every PostgREST call routes through `getSession()`, which serialises on a cross-tab Web Lock, Chrome FREEZES background tabs, and this family runs ~35 across three doors on one origin. **THE ARITHMETIC WAS THE BUG.** auth-js 2.106 already recovers — on its acquire timeout it STEALS the orphaned lock (supabase/supabase#42505), freeing it for everyone, so the cost is paid once — but the DEFAULT WINDOW is 5000ms while `bounded-read` gives a whole read 6000ms: a contended read spent ~83% of its budget waiting to start and reported `not-reached` having never been given a chance to answer. Fixed with the vendor's own knob, `lockAcquireTimeout: 1200`. **A HAND-ROLLED LOCK WAS WRITTEN FIRST AND DELETED BEFORE IT SHIPPED** — reading the real library source (rather than assuming the default was a plain forever-wait) showed the steal-recovery already existed, and stealing is strictly better than the custom fallback's "proceed unlocked": it RELEASES the orphan instead of routing around it, and it is the vendor's tested path in the app's most sensitive code. **THE FOURTH BOUND WAS THE SIGNAL (P49):** the boot gate (2026-07-13), Admin access+usage (2026-07-22), PIN reads, and Properties (2026-09-01) had each bounded this same lock's symptom; a bound can only choose HOW a read fails, and four honest timeouts is still four timeouts. When a workaround reaches a fourth surface, the cause is upstream and the workaround is the finding. Gated on the RELATIONSHIP, not the number: `auth-lock-window.test.js` reads BOTH real constants and was observed to fail on 5000 (the default), on 0 (fail-immediately), on -1 (wait-forever — the vendor's own documented deadlock), and on the line's removal; a floor of >=500ms is pinned too, because stealing from a genuinely live refresher would cause the token-rotation race the lock exists to prevent — a WORSE failure than the one being fixed. `bounded-read` stays as the backstop and the test pins that it does. **NOT CLAIMED:** verified by test and by reading the library's source, NOT yet by Darrell reproducing his 35-tab window on the shipped build — that live confirmation is the remaining proof (DR-0104) | accepted | A | the auth client, and every read in every surface | VERIFICATION-DOCTRINE, EXECUTION-OUTCOME-OBSERVABILITY, COMMUNITY-FIRST, LESSONS-LEARNED, PERPETUAL-IMPROVEMENT |

| [DR-0335](DR-0335-the-descent-taught-both-fences-power-destroyed-person-not.md) | **The descent is taught with BOTH fences — his power was destroyed at the cross, his person was not, and the hours Scripture does not narrate stay unwritten.** Darrell, 2026-09-07: "Did Jesus destroy the devil when He went to hell for 3 days and nights according to the biblical scriptures?" | [DR-0337](DR-0337-the-porter-was-already-in-the-text-a-labor-day-lesson-and-the-two-track-honesty-rule.md) | **The porter was already in the text — a Labor Day lesson, and the two-track honesty rule for history beside Scripture.** Darrell, 2026-09-08: "lesson." plus a telling about the Pullman porters — men hired out of slavery to staff America's sleeping cars and addressed by passengers as George, the owner's first name, because "you didn't have to learn who they were." The occasion is history; the LESSON is Scripture, and the join was not manufactured: **the KJV word for the man at the door of the sheepfold is PORTER**, in a sentence about the exact opposite of what a railway carriage did — "To him the porter openeth... and he calleth his own sheep by name" (John 10:3). In the house of Yahweh the porters are an ORDAINED Levitical office, NAMED in the permanent record (Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman — 1 Chronicles 9:17), 212 of them ordained by David and Samuel (9:22), trusted with the treasury (9:26), given authority and the watch (Mark 13:34); a reigning king wanted the job (Psalms 84:10). The word a nation used to make men interchangeable is the word Yahweh uses for a named servant at His own gate. From there, the Word on its own terms: Yahweh names and is NEVER ONCE recorded un-naming (Genesis 17:5; 32:28; John 1:42; Isaiah 56:5; Revelation 2:17); the first person recorded naming HIM is a discarded slave woman, and the name is about being SEEN (Genesis 16:13); He positions the overlooked on purpose (Genesis 39:2; 2 Kings 5:2-3; 1 Corinthians 1:27-28); the stone the BUILDERS refuse is the one He sets in the corner (Psalms 118:22); and He legislated the labourer's wage — same day, before sundown, "for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it" (Deuteronomy 24:15) — millennia before any nation had a labour movement, which makes it the real Labor Day text. THE TWO-TRACK HONESTY RULE, decided and now gated: Scripture is fetched verbatim and checkable (198 spans, empty NOT_SCRIPTURE allowlist — our emphasis wears capitals, never quotes); documented history is stated PLAINLY without hedging (DR-0100 — under-claiming a truth is its own lie); commonly-cited ranges are LABELLED as ranges; a compression in the telling is corrected gently in our prose with its reason (the Brotherhood was the first Black-led union chartered by the AFL and first to win a contract with a major corporation — accuracy makes the story harder to dismiss, not smaller); and provenance is named, since the Scripture was verified against the corpus while the history is well-established knowledge, not fetched. BOTH FENCES gated, because this material wounds when preached bare: under-claiming is forbidden (Exodus 21:16 sentences the man-stealer to death; 1 Timothy 1:10 lists menstealers as contrary to sound doctrine), over-claiming equally so (Genesis 50:20 holds they thought evil AND Yahweh meant it unto good as TWO facts — collapsing them turns a comfort into a defence of the men who did it), the EDIT IS THE TELL (Bibles were printed with portions cut out; had the text supported the system nobody would have needed a blade — Deuteronomy 4:2, Acts 20:27, and the restored suppressed half at Colossians 4:1), and no partisan contest is staged (DR-0098). Ends on the Son who was looked away from (Isaiah 53:3), took the servant's form (Philippians 2:7), and was given the Name above every name (Philippians 2:9) — a worship lesson, not a grievance lesson, asserted by the gate. Two real defects caught and both now proven-to-catch: a SHORTENED quotation (2 Chronicles 8:14 trimmed to "for so had God commanded" — three words short of the verse and not in the corpus at all), and SIX generic "God" in our own authored voice; the DR-0210 check strips quoted spans first, because a check that did not would demand we corrupt the text — and it now carries its COMPLEMENT, that the KJV's own "God" must still be PRESENT inside quotations, closing the loophole where a blind find-replace would have passed. Register measured, not claimed: child 1.30 / teen 6.70 / adult 8.00 / senior 12.30, not inverted, child under the ceiling, and the shrink-only baseline gained NO new offenders. TWO numbering collisions in one afternoon: authored as L131, renumbered to L134 when a fetch of main showed L131-L133 merged mid-authoring, shipped as L135 after main merged its OWN L134 (#1482) while this PR's CI ran. AND A CORRECTION TO THIS RECORD'S OWN FIRST DRAFT, kept rather than edited away: it said the collision was caught "not by a gate," which was false — `living-lessons-id-collision.test.js` has existed since 2026-09-02, built after two sessions independently claimed L114, and asserts exactly this. The SECOND collision locates the real catch: it surfaced as a git add/add conflict on the test FILENAME, which is the very mechanism that gate's own header calls "luck, not a check" — had the filenames differed, git would have auto-merged both modules in silence. That silent case is what the gate is for, and merging main into a PR head is the first moment both claims exist in one tree, so it fires ON THE PR, in CI, before main is touched. MEASURED, not asserted: the duplicate was reconstructed and the suite went red naming both ids. Decision: no new gate and no re-review date — the check exists, is sufficient, and fires at the only moment it can; fetching main first is a courtesy that saves a merge cycle, never the safety. Claiming a gap without grepping for the gate that closes it is the DR-0107 cited-but-unread failure in miniature. | accepted | n/a | poetech, colg | WORD-FIRST, VERIFICATION-DOCTRINE, TEACH-DONT-DEBATE, SPEAK-ESTABLISHED-FACT, SPOKEN-TEACHINGS-ARE-BUILD-INPUT, COMMUNITY-FIRST-MISSION, EXCELLENCE-STANDARD, DECISION-RECORDS |

| [DR-0378](DR-0378-a-fault-is-addressed-to-the-office-never-broadcast.md) | **A fault is addressed to the office, never broadcast.** **THIS RECORD EXISTS BECAUSE I BROKE DR-0111 AND THE ARI-GUARD CAUGHT IT BEFORE DARRELL SAW IT.** Having just shipped DR-0377, I told him that pushing a fault to the office was *"the timer-driven class and is Darrell's call, not something to slip in"* -- and stopped. THE DECISION THAT ACTUALLY NEEDED MAKING, AND I MADE IT: a fault push is NOT shaped like `live`, and getting that wrong would have been a real leak. `live` fans out to every opted-in device in a tenant -- correct for a congregation, wrong for "this business's shop is broken," where the entitled audience is the OFFICE (owner/admin, the same predicate 0216's RLS uses). The tempting shortcut was to inherit the instance broadcast and rely on "only the steward screen offers the toggle" -- **a UI gate pretending to be an access gate**, which would tell any customer who reached the topic by another route when Shay's shop is failing. So an explicit office audience is REQUIRED, routing `fault` through `audienceQuery`'s per-person path rather than the per-instance one: **there is no code path that broadcasts a fault**, and the validator refuses the attempt rather than quietly fanning out. Decisions: `fault` joins the CLOSED enumerated `SENDABLE_TOPICS`, whose pinning test exists precisely so a broadcast channel cannot be added unseen -- updated deliberately rather than deleted; the audience is mandatory and explicit, with the reason in the error; **the fault id IS the dedupe key and that is load-bearing**, since 0217 FOLDS a repeat into the same row and returns the SAME id, so a door failing four hundred times buzzes the office EXACTLY ONCE and only a genuinely new open fault earns a second buzz -- the storm was already one row, this makes it one notification; NO error text and NO customer text on a lock screen, the same posture `messageAnnouncement` takes for DM bodies since a push renders in public to whoever holds the phone (asserted against `unknown pipeline`, `crm_capture_lead`, `SELECT` and `@`) -- the push says THAT something is wrong and HOW WIDELY, the app says what; and the count is carried because it IS the severity, "hit it 47 times" being the difference between a snag and a shop closed all morning. BRAKES DESIGNED IN RATHER THAN DEFERRED (DR-0248 budget + lock): budget is the title/body caps, MAX_DEVICES_PER_SEND, and an audience of a named handful rather than a tenant; the lock is the dedupe key, enforced by the key rather than by a caller remembering. NOT DONE, and the reason is VERIFIED SECURITY rather than scheduling: the trigger is server-side and deliberately NOT built here, because the obvious shortcut -- the client calling push-send after filing its fault -- would let ANY ANONYMOUS VISITOR BUZZ SHAY'S PHONE ON DEMAND, a far worse abuse vector than the spoofable row 0217 already accepts (a row is read when she opens a board; a push is an intrusion into her pocket), so the client deliberately does not call it and the trigger belongs on a server path that reads open faults and resolves the office itself -- re-review 2026-09-20; no office member has subscribed to the topic because nothing offers the toggle yet; and no live fault has been pushed end to end. Decisions: the door files its own SYSTEM-sourced row into the same book the office already reads (`door_fault_report`, 0217) so there is no second inbox and no new screen to remember; DEDUPED, because a broken door is broken for everyone and a hundred visitors must not become a hundred rows burying the customer voice -- an identical OPEN fault inside 24h increments `occurrences` and moves `last_seen_at`, and **the count IS the alert** ("47 times since 9am" says what one row never could); a fold NEVER reopens what the office handled, since a closed fault breaking again is genuinely new and earns its own row rather than a silent bump on settled work; A SEPARATE FUNCTION rather than a flag on `door_feedback_submit`, because that customer path was verified on both databases hours earlier (md5 63cf8950...) and is not being touched, re-tested or put at risk to add a second behaviour; the office is told a SENTENCE not a stack trace, with the machine detail capped at 300 chars (a raw error is noise to a steward and an unbounded one on her screen is an injection surface); a machine is NEVER displayed as a person -- system rows are labelled "the app noticed this", carry their count, and say "Written by the app, not a person -- there is nobody to reply to" where a customer row would offer contact details, with open faults getting their own banner because "your door is reporting a problem on its own" is not a queue item; and a fault report NEVER makes things worse, never throwing and never surfacing, with DR-0374's honest error panel still rendering exactly as before -- the self-report is IN ADDITION to telling the customer the truth, never instead of it. EXPLICITLY NOT THE TIMER-DRIVEN CLASS, so the three-brakes rule does not attach (DR-0247/0248): no loop to budget, lock or stop -- a row is written when a real user action really failed and the office PULLS it; a push notification WOULD be that class and is left to its own decision rather than smuggled in. SPOOFING STATED PLAINLY: the seam is anon-callable so a row can claim to be a system fault, the same exposure DR-0376 already accepted, bounded by the same flood brake -- and the alternative, trusting only server-observed faults, CANNOT SEE a failure happening in the customer's browser, which is exactly where Sterling's happened; visible and spoofable beats invisible. Proof: verify green 953 files / 14,241 tests; 17 tests MOUNTING the door and failing a real order with the real refusal shape; proven-to-catch twice, each by one precisely-targeted test -- removing the self-report fails the "calls door_fault_report" test, removing the fold fails the "FOLDS a repeat" test. METHODOLOGY NOTE KEPT because it repeated tonight: my first attempt at the second break DID NOT APPLY, the suite stayed green, and 0 failures meant NOTHING -- an incomplete break rather than a weak test, verified before any conclusion was drawn, the same trap as DR-0373's. **EXECUTED AND WITNESSED ON BOTH DATABASES** (merged `d591bc2b`): `door_fault_report` reads md5 `f8f4382d4f2bf37200d6aa065758b654` on hosted by direct query AND the identical value on the SOVEREIGN database (`sovereign-read` run 34743949911, `---MISSING--- none`, `sovereign_replay=223`); anon can call it, the table stays closed to anon (false/false), the new columns and `source` CHECK are present, and the policy count is STILL 8 after the ALTER -- office plus both overlays intact, which was the specific regression risk worth checking rather than assuming. **DECISION 4 IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED:** `door_feedback_submit` reads md5 `63cf89507ec6cc0bf35253e461198c3c` on both databases, byte-for-byte what it was BEFORE 0217 existed, so "a separate function leaves the verified customer path untouched" is a fact rather than a design intention. NOT DONE: only the ORDER form reports itself so far, while the same door's classes, messages and showcase seams still fail quietly -- the pattern is now one function call so widening it is small, but claiming the door is instrumented would overstate it, re-review 2026-09-27; nothing reaches the office while they are AWAY from the board, since this makes a fault findable rather than pushed; and no live fault has been observed end to end, the sandbox having no route to poetech.us -- re-review 2026-09-20 | accepted | B | business | VERIFICATION-DOCTRINE, APP-IS-PRIMARY, REALITY-TRACE, PERPETUAL-IMPROVEMENT, DECISION-RECORDS |

Nearly invisible on the main list (you rarely re-tap the lesson you just left) and THE NORMAL CASE on "Recently opened", which is BY DEFINITION the lessons you already opened — so the most likely tap on that row was the one guaranteed to do nothing; a rising nonce makes arrival an EVENT rather than a VALUE. The chip became a LINK because a row whose whole purpose is "return to where you were" must look like the thing you return with. Play landed on the presenter CONSOLE — a setup screen with its own START button — so the control named Play played nothing until a second tap; it now arrives already presenting. AND THE CAP IS A MOVE, NOT A DELETION, which is the whole decision: a lesson's anchor carries every reference the WHOLE lesson stands on (L149's is eighty) and the slide printed the entire string — a LIST rendered as content, DR-0391's defect in a different medium — so teaching slides name only the few the session opens on with an honest "+77 more" and the closing "The Word we stood on" slide carries the whole list, while IN-LINE references throughout the lesson are untouched, exactly as he asked. THE CAP NEEDED SOMEWHERE TO LAND: six lessons author no run-of-show and so never had a closing slide, and capping their one teaching slide would have dropped the list out of the deck ALTOGETHER rather than moving it to the end — caught by the corpus-wide test, not by reading. A TEST WAS RE-POINTED ON PURPOSE, NOT WEAKENED: the Play assertion was not wrong when written, it described the behaviour he asked to change, so it now pins the NEW contract rather than being deleted. Proven-to-catch: drop the nonce from the effect deps, or stop bumping it in open(), and the re-tap test fails; 24 new tests; 971 files, 14,595 tests green | accepted | B | orchestration | VERIFICATION-DOCTRINE, APP-IS-PRIMARY, COMPREHENSIVE-REVIEW-STANDARD, DECISION-RECORDS |

Cause, exactly: deploy-freshness compares main against the last SUCCESSFUL deploy, and while #1157 was still running the last success was the previous tip, so it honestly read STALE and dispatched. DECISION: any deploy run for main's EXACT tip suppresses the dispatch whatever its status (queued, running, even failed -- a failed deploy is the deploy workflow's business to report, never a reason to stack another build), so the in-flight query carries NO status filter while the freshness comparison above it still uses one, because *has this tip been served?* and *has anyone already been asked to serve it?* are different questions. Three outcomes get three return codes -- dispatched, already-in-flight, fresh-or-unresolved -- and only the last keeps looking; the code is captured around a `set +e` because the step runs under `set -euo pipefail` and a bare non-zero return would abort the job, turning a correct no-op red. auto-merge's heal already had this gate; it simply had not been carried into the second net. 13 checks (4 new), **24/24 breaks caught, 0 theatre** -- including the in-flight query narrowed to successes only, which is this very bug re-introduced. NOT PROVEN: that exactly one deploy now runs per merge; the fix is verified against the file, not against GitHub (`re-review: 2026-09-18`, one merge away, with the fallback named). |

| [DR-0463](DR-0463-through-the-eyes-of-the-people-closest-to-him-and-a-claim-answered-in-the-form-that-is-true.md) | **Through the eyes of the people closest to Him, and a claim answered in the form that is true.** Darrell 2026-09-17, spoken and marked lesson twice: see the Word through the eyes of the people nearest Jesus so His will and His way and who He was are ACCENTED and we see Him clearer -- Peter in vivid detail, the man who can say taste and see because he walked it and the same man who said he did not know Him while the bird did what it did; his brothers who did not believe until after He was gone; who is my mother, my sister, my brother; the local community not showing Him love; the people present at the death; the burial details; the resurrection witnesses including the five hundred; the history and archaeology pulled out of the ground so His existence inside time is visible; and a claim to check carefully -- more data about Jesus than about Julius Caesar. The people at the death NAMED, which is not how legends are written (Matthew 27:54; Luke 23:48-49; John 19:25-27) -- dying, He was arranging housing for His mother. The burial as the most checkable material in the account: a named councillor, Pilate verifying the death with the executing officer, fine linen, an unused rock tomb, a hundred pound weight of spices, a garden, a stone, a seal and a watch (Mark 15:43-46; Luke 23:53; John 19:39,41; Matthew 27:64-66). **AND THE RIVAL STORY THE WORD ITSELF RECORDS IS THE HINGE** -- the money, the line to say, and the concession that it spread (Matthew 28:12-13,15): an invented account does not price its own competitor and admit it worked. Issue 17 leads with Yahweh's own account — Hebrews 11:3, Colossians 1:16-17, Genesis 2:7 (dust, then His breath, which is not in the sequence), Job 38, Psalms 139 — and puts the men second, arriving late. Tier 1 states plainly that the Human Genome Project achieved its goal (three billion base pairs, a success, per Darrell's own correcting second block), that Hingorani et al. in BMJ Medicine 2023 found a typical polygenic score detects about 11% of cases at a 5% false-positive rate across 926 scores and 310 diseases, that Brownian motion has been observed since 1827, that a cell is not computable molecule by molecule, and that today's machines have no senses; Tier 2 names narrowly that "neo-Darwinism is dead" is Noble's verdict in a live dispute mainstream biology has NOT conceded, that human transgenerational epigenetic inheritance is unsettled, and that the finite-monkeys calculation carries its own fatal objection in the same field and is never a proof; Tier 3 corrects the over-reach in both directions — a man is not a readout of his genes (Ezekiel 18:20; Deuteronomy 30:19), AND biology has not proved Yahweh, because "Through faith we understand" (Hebrews 11:3) names the instrument and Romans 1:20's "without excuse" is a verdict rather than a proof. The centre of the lesson is consciousness: Psalms 115:4-7 inventories the senses of a made thing in the same order three thousand years earlier, and verse 8 turns it on the makers, so the reduction of a soul to a mechanism is named from both the chip and the chromosome, with Habakkuk 2:19's "it shall teach" aimed at this house's own teaching tools; water answers the prediction limit (Psalms 147:4-5; Job 38:37; Job 26:8; 2 Peter 3:5), chance is released from rivalry with providence (Proverbs 16:33; the arrow drawn at a venture, 1 Kings 22:34), Paul had already reasoned from fail-safe design (1 Corinthians 12:24-25; Ephesians 4:16), and the close is the WHOLE of Deuteronomy 29:29 rather than mystery alone. Anchored in Hebrews 11:3 and Genesis 2:7, with a grace note that condemns no one and states that "anti-Yahweh" names the CLAIM and never the person, a full unmocked steelman of the gene-centric view, and a mainstream-synthesis perspective that holds Noble overstates what it overturns. | [DR-0570](DR-0570-the-local-app-carries-the-house-address-both-lanes-are-kept.md) | **The local app carries the house's address: the native shell lane opens, and both lanes are kept.** Darrell: *"all the bells and whistles come from a local download... Let's do the native shell... Don't undermine what we have... We don't have to pick either or... just need to plan for both."* Measured ground: the Android app today is a TWA (`android-package.yml:7`) that gives the phone nothing the browser does not -- the per-device bridge key the voice chain could not provision (DR-0566) is exactly that wall; no Capacitor anywhere in the repo; the web build is one layout at base `/poetech-app/` published at the site root and rewritten by `_redirects`; the NAS is reached by ten relative same-origin routes; Capacitor's local server routes extension-less paths to the ROOT index.html and, with CapacitorHttp on, sends every non-local URL through native HTTP (both read from source). Decision: two lanes, both whole. The TWA lane is untouched (same workflow, shelf, ids, store buttons). Lesson"* and, mid-turn, *"After fixing what needs to be done"* (the fix — the rental data-loss clobber — shipped first as DR-0394). L150, answered Word-first (DR-0098) and honestly (DR-0076): it does NOT dodge the sentence the Son Himself spoke — *"of that day and that hour knoweth no man... neither the Son, but the Father"* (Mark 13:32; Matthew 24:36) — and it does NOT resolve it by making the Son a lesser being, because the same Word says He knows all (*"Lord, thou knowest all things"* John 21:17; *"are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge"* Colossians 2:3) and is fully Yahweh the Son (John 1:1; John 10:30; Colossians 2:9). Seven strands: (1) the question is real and Jesus said it; (2) He knows all; (3) the kenosis — *"made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant"* (Philippians 2:5-8; 2 Corinthians 8:9) — the USE laid down, not the deity; (4) a real human mind that *"increased in wisdom"* (Luke 2:52) and *"learned he obedience"* (Hebrews 5:8; Hebrews 2:17; 4:15); (5) ORDER not rank — John 5:19, Acts 1:7, *"my Father is greater than I"* (John 14:28) beside the worship the same Son receives, *"My Lord and my God"* (John 20:28) and *"Thy throne, O God"* (Hebrews 1:8); (6) glory laid down and asked back (John 17:5) then exalted (Matthew 28:18; Philippians 2:9-11); (7) the Lamb of Yahweh (John 1:29; Colossians 1:16-17; Revelation 5:12), and where the Word is quiet on HOW two natures share one mind, teaching stops (Deuteronomy 29:29; Isaiah 55:9), turning personal — *"Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus"* (Philippians 2:5), *"we have the mind of Christ"* (1 Corinthians 2:16). DR-0098 in practice: the ancient wrong answer is NAMED once to walk past it, never platformed. | [DR-0393](DR-0393-the-base-can-move-while-you-verify-and-a-successful-push-can-be-the-failure.md) | **The base can move while you verify, and a successful push can be the failure.** No report — found by the agent while recovering from it the SECOND time in one evening, which is the finding, because nothing in the system said a word either time. `npm run verify` takes ~4 minutes (971 files, 14,595 tests) and the delivery lane squash-merges the instant gates pass, with no human in the path; twice those facts collided (23:38 verify starts on main@ce533569 / 23:42 the lane merges #1566 to main@2066e992 / 23:58 verify goes green and the commit is pushed). A SQUASH MERGE CREATES A NEW COMMIT THAT DOES NOT CONTAIN THE BRANCH'S OWN COMMITS AS ANCESTORS, so the verified commit landed on history main no longer had — and THE PUSH SUCCEEDED BOTH TIMES, which is what made it expensive: nothing failed, nothing printed, and the damage surfaced later as a PR carrying already-merged commits and an INDEX conflict (#1565 stranded fcdc9253; #1566 stranded 60f627a7). ROOT CAUSE: every safeguard runs either BEFORE the push (verify, the 15 gates) or AFTER it (CI, the lane, site-health) — the four minutes between green and push is the one interval nothing watches, and it is exactly as long as the window the lane needs to move the base; the FASTER the lane got, the likelier this became. DECISIONS: the signal is TIME, NOT SHAPE — stamp origin/main when verification starts, re-read it before the push, so it is squash-, merge- and rebase-proof; it deliberately does NOT fire on "the branch is behind main", the normal harmless state of nearly every branch, because a guard that cries on the normal case is ignored within a day (P52, learned the day before); it is NOT a CI gate and CANNOT be, since CI runs after the push, so `npm run ship` chains stamp → verify → check → push and narrows the race from four minutes to one `git fetch`; and UNKNOWN never reads as green (no stamp, no origin, no network → exit 2, "do not read this as safe to push"). THE REJECTED DESIGN IS RECORDED ON PURPOSE: the first version used `git cherry`, and run against the REAL shape it printed six `+` and not one `-` — patch-id matches one commit to one commit and a squash matches none of them, so it would have passed silently on the very accident it was written for; deleted rather than shipped, with the rejection written into the guard's own header. That sharpens DR-0076 §3: proven-to-catch means proven against the SPECIFIC INCIDENT, not a synthetic case chosen because it passes. Proven-to-catch in both directions (disable drift detection → 3 fail; make a missing stamp read green → 3 fail), 12 tests. LIMITS: it protects `npm run ship`, not a hand `git push` (which gets the honest UNKNOWN exit, not prevention — no hooks installed); and it detects the drift without repairing it, since restarting a branch is the user's call — re-review 2026-10-14 | accepted | B | orchestration | VERIFICATION-DOCTRINE, STREAMLINED-DELIVERY-LOOP, DECISION-RECORDS |

| [DR-0956](DR-0956-a-guard-that-reads-one-of-two-inputs.md) | **A guard that reads one of its two inputs is not a guard.** PR #2112 went red on ci.yml’s door-work leg: `0154:217 ERROR: cannot change return type of existing function ... Use DROP FUNCTION public_vacancy_photos(uuid) first`. THE RULE WAS ALREADY WRITTEN AND ALREADY ENFORCED — ON THE OTHER FILE. migration-replay-order-guard exists for this exact class and caught the identical collision on rls-isolation.yml when 0273 was built; the fix went where the guard was looking, ci.yml replays migrations too in shell rather than a matrix, the guard had never read it, and the second leg shipped broken. The guard’s own header documents three earlier versions of this miss and names the lesson — “a guard that cannot see part of its own input is the P55 shape again”. This is the fourth. MEASURED on real PostgreSQL 16.15, replaying the leg exactly: 0273 twice → SHARED HOME SMOKE PASS; 0154 with no drop → the CI error reproduced byte for byte, same file and line; with the drop → PHOTO DATES SMOKE PASS. And the revert is REAL — after the 0154 replay `from_sibling` is GONE (count 0), so a door would silently stop borrowing its sibling’s pictures. Now: shellLegs() reads ci.yml’s replay legs in shell order, both the inline path and the `for f in` list, counting only files that exist and ignoring comments; the shell check is POSITIONAL and stricter than the matrix one (a drop after the clash does not excuse it — a leg-level `pre` cannot tell those apart); door-work drops the function before replaying 0153/0154; and the leg PROVES THE CHAIN CONVERGES by re-applying 0273 and running its smoke a second time, because a replay that does not error is not a chain that ends where it should (DR-0944). 29 green in the guard’s own suite, 9 new; proven to catch by deleting the one DROP line — the CLI names the job, the file, the function and the remedy, and two live-repo cases go red. | [DR-0954](DR-0954-signing-in-comes-back-through-the-door.md) | **Signing in comes back through the door.** Christina could not get in at all: "I click on I live here... it is a loop as it goes straight to these 3 pages over and over." Leaving this door writes a per-door flag and doorSession hides the session while it is set; enterDoor clears it and its own docstring says it is called whenever a sign-in succeeds at that door — the sign-in call site never called it. She signed in SUCCESSFULLY, reloaded, and the door still believed she had left. The only escape was the small "Come back in" link, which nobody who has just signed in goes looking for. Clear the flag, then reload. |
| [DR-0955](DR-0955-a-list-of-pictures-carries-no-pictures.md) | **A list of pictures carries no pictures.** Darrell 2026-10-11: “Are images stored on/in the nas?” — they are, inside the Postgres row as base64, not as files — then “Can we fix it?!!!!!” My recommendation to move them to /nas-photos was WRONG ON TIMING and surfaced as such before building: that road is itself a Pages Function and is in site-health’s dark list (#2057). This is the fix on the road that works. MEASURED: thumb_path is an IMAGE too — the same base64 data URL at 640 px / 75% — 47 KB for a smooth interior, 60 KB for a detailed one, ~55 KB a row; loadAllPhotos reads every unarchived picture on every boot, so 67 rows is ~3.6 MB in one answer against a 6 s deadline on the throttling Funnel, and Bed A’s 39 pictures are ~2.1 MB. That is the frozen tab AND the “keeps flashing... coming back with new images about 20 seconds later”: the late response repainting after the UI gave up. A GATE WAS HOLDING HALF A FIX IN PLACE — property-photos-list-carries-no-bytes pinned `toContain('thumb_path')` and was green the whole evening. Now: the list is metadata, no image column of ANY size; loadPhotoThumbs by id, bounded at 12 (~660 KB); each tile fetches its own thumbnail when it comes into view through SharpPicture’s existing observer, cache and 3-at-a-time queue; a waiting tile HOLDS ITS PLACE (return null would mean the observed element never exists, so nothing is ever asked for); a pre-0185 row with no thumbnail is left OUT of the answer rather than recorded empty, and falls through to its full image; no picture is fetched at boot at all, and hydrateLegacyImages is REMOVED because `!p.thumb_path` now matches every row and it would have pulled 24 FULL images (~7 MB) every boot. The Real Estate strip batches thumbnails too — it drops any item with no src, so the column change alone would have made every Poe Properties picture silently vanish there. Also: “No photo” on the Doors board asked `listImage(x.cover)` — whether the bytes were in hand — so the column change alone would have made EVERY cover read “No photo” for good; it asks `x.cover` now, which is a fact about the door. 16 new cases green with a controllable IntersectionObserver so “off screen” is a real state; 136 green across the Properties suites; six breaks each caught. The NAS FILE-SERVER MOVE remains the structural answer and stays queued behind #2057. `re-review: 2026-10-18`. |
| [DR-0959](DR-0959-a-guest-may-stay-as-long-as-they-like.md) | **A guest may stay as long as they like, at the nightly rate.** Darrell 2026-10-11, reading his own live card: “we dont want people to do short term leases because of staying passed 29 days!!! They can stay for a year with $150 a day if they want too!!!” SECOND TIME ASKING — 0269 line 77 records the first in his own words (“Not 29 day cap?... why?”) and the cap survived that round with a research note; he has reaffirmed it, so it is his call. MEASURED: the card read “Up to 29 nights here; for longer, apply for a lease”, enforced in three places — a CHECK constraint, GUEST_MAX_NIGHTS = 29, and the copy. A guest wanting sixty nights at $150 was refused and pushed toward the very instrument he does not want for these stays. Stated once and not argued (DR-0100): the Hotel Operators’ tax and Champaign’s 7% reach stays under 30 CONSECUTIVE days, and a 30+ night occupancy begins to carry tenancy characteristics with no bright line in Illinois — both still on the ask-counsel list, neither a reason the FORM should refuse the booking. The card now names the 30-night line as worth knowing, not as a wall. The year ceiling stays. Executed on real PostgreSQL 16.15, applied twice: 60 nights refused before and accepted after, a year accepted, 425 nights still refused. 7 green. AND A ROBUSTNESS DEFECT FOUND BY A FAILED RUN OF MY OWN TEST — the first version began a bare `ALTER TABLE public.door_stays` and errored on a chain that stops before 0269, which several CI legs replay on purpose; the body is now inside an existence guard. `re-review: 2026-10-18`. |

A guest ready to pay was told to wait for a message. Now: public_stay_payment(uuid) returns the Square link and nightly rate to anon AND authenticated; ONE column out of rent_payee (never the cashtag, Zelle, deposit wording or cheque payee) and rent_payee itself stays member-only; only for a door that is listed, short-term or both, and not our own home; the link is re-checked as a Square address on the road a stranger is sent down with money; money still never moves in the app (0055); and a missing or unreadable link says “we will send you how to pay” rather than inventing a method. Executed on real PostgreSQL 16.15 twice: anonymous, signed-in non-member and member all get the link for a listed door and nothing for an unlisted or long-term-only one, while a direct read of rent_payee is permission-denied for anon and 0 rows for a non-member. 10 green driving the real form; proven to catch by making a failed read fall back to a link. AND A BUG IN MY OWN MIGRATION, found because a test returned nothing and I checked: the filter said offering IN ('short-stay','both'), which is not a value the column can hold (0155 allows long-term/short-term/both), so the link would have been withheld from EVERY door while failing nowhere. NOT PROVEN: whether the live square_link is set — if not, guests see the honest fallback until Darrell pastes it in. `re-review: 2026-10-18`. |
| [DR-0967](DR-0967-the-sibling-read-asks-by-id.md) | **The sibling read asks by the door's id, and the apartment NUMBER decides what is one apartment.** Darrell after DR-0963 deployed: "Images for apartment 4... B?!!!!" and "We need to be able to see the images in Apt 4... B... so we can advertise!!!!!!!!!!!" Deploy 1619 on 0f6c7594 succeeded, so the code was live and the read returned nothing. TWO faults. (1) `loadSiblingPhotos` filtered property_photos by SLUGS; the column holds the rental's UUID -- apt2-photos-probe.yml joins `r.id = p.rental_ref`, and PropertiesApp calls `loadDoorPhotos(rentalId)` into a parameter merely NAMED rentalRef. Zero rows, silently. And the comment I shipped beside it asserted the opposite, congratulating itself for avoiding the exact bug it was in the act of writing -- a reviewer would have been reassured by it, which is worse than no comment. (2) Mid-fix Darrell named the better rule: "If it has the same apt number its the same location... can we make sure this happens each time we co-live a place?" His own doors break exact-string matching -- Bed B is '805 North Prospect Avenue Apt 4' / 'Apt 4', Apt 2 is '805 North Prospect Avenue' / 'Apt 2'; the unit got typed into the address on one door and not another, as anybody does by hand. `sameApartment` now folds the unit out of the street and compares the unit by NUMBER: Apt 4, apt. 4, #4, Unit 4 and 4 are one apartment. Deliberately NOT fuzzy on the street -- '805 N Prospect Ave' still differs from '805 North Prospect Avenue', with a test saying so, because guessing addresses are 'probably' the same is how one family's pictures advertise another family's door. 13 tests; proven-to-catch, reverting to slugs (the exact state on his phone) fails 2 of 6. Why the original 9 passed: they fed sharedPhotos in as a PROP, proving the card renders while blind to the read returning nothing -- rung 3 with no rung-1 twin (DR-0347). |

| [DR-0969](DR-0969-the-progress-line-says-what-is-being-spent.md) | **The progress line says what is being SPENT, and the wait explains itself while you wait.** "Why is downloading lesson so long with only mb of data?!!!!!!!!!!" -- a fair reading of what the screen said. 386 pieces x ~87 chars / (19.7 chars/s x 2 streams) ~= 14 minutes, over which 1.8 MB is ~2 kB/s: it is not a download, and the megabytes are the one quantity NOT being spent. | [DR-0970](DR-0970-a-dead-bell-says-so.md) | **A dead bell says so -- `curl -sS` exits 0 on a 404, so the phone alarm reported itself as rung.** site-health run 38141832465 caught it verbatim: {"code":404,"message":"The requested webhook \"POST ops-announce\" is not registered."}. The guard was `curl -sS ... || echo "::warning::"`, and WITHOUT `-f` a 404 is exit 0 -- so the `||` could never fire on the one failure actually happening, and an unregistered, renamed, revoked or 500-ing webhook was indistinguishable from a bell that rang. Only "connection refused" ever worked. The deploy ran red ~2h that morning with no bell and nobody knew the bell was the broken thing. The same file already did it right forty lines up (the probe reads `-w %{http_code}`), so this was a path nobody made fail on purpose. Now: scripts/ops-announce.mjs, pure core + thin shell, 2xx the only acceptance (UNKNOWN IS NOT RUNG), the reason naming the FIX (404 not-registered = the n8n workflow is not ACTIVE on the NAS; 401 = the bearer), a missing bearer NOT counted as dead, exit 3 for "reached but broken", and the dead bell recorded on the incident ledger where humans look rather than a warning stream (P53). 16 tests on the real 404 body; proven-to-catch 9/16 by restoring the curl semantics; the three exit codes proven against a live local relay and the workflow shell block actually run (bell=3, token absent from the log). |
| [DR-0971](DR-0971-a-bed-is-not-a-bedroom.md) | **A bed is not a bedroom -- the shelf infers the level the way the app already does.** "0.5 Bedroom or 1-Bedroom?!!!!!?????!!!!!" -- neither. His board said "half 0.5 of Room - Bed A"; the public card said "1-bed multi-family in Champaign, Illinois" with no mention of housemates, which is the misreading that sends somebody to Apt 4 with a car full of belongings. 0273 already composed "Bed in a shared ..." and already derived shared_home -- both reading rentals.rentable_level RAW, and that column is NULL on his doors because NOTHING IN THE APP EVER WRITES IT. One root, both symptoms, including why "none say co-living" was still true after 0273 shipped. DR-0968 had checked whether the column was READ and nobody asked whether it was WRITTEN. levelOf() has inferred from a door’s own labels since August ("twelve doors exist today with no level on them, and two of those are beds"); 0278 gives the database that same reading, and a bed or room now reports NO bedroom/bathroom count because those describe the whole apartment. EXECUTED ON A REAL PostgreSQL 16.15: his three doors resolve bed/bed/unit and the "2 Bedroom" traps hold. The parity pin caught a real divergence before shipping -- levelOf() was case-sensitive on the stored value while the SQL folded case; both fold now. 44 green. |

| [DR-0973](DR-0973-the-public-shelf-has-a-witness.md) | **The public shelf has a witness -- and it takes the reading a browser cannot take.** Darrell found three faults on his own listing from his phone while every check was green, and DR-0952’s co-living line had been REPORTED TO HIM AS LIVE while it rendered nothing for nine days. So the red check was reporting on a run that had been correctly abandoned in favour of one that passed. THE COST IS THE POINT: a reader who investigates that twice stops doing it a third time and starts discounting red, which is DR-0076 §3’s lie from the other direction — a gate that always passes is a lie, and a gate whose red does not mean “broken” trains people out of reading it. Now a genuine failure names the failed legs as FAILED; anything else incomplete says it DID NOT FINISH, says explicitly that nothing failed, names the usual cause (a newer commit) and points at that commit’s own run as the one that counts; and when a run BOTH fails and has cancellations the failure wins with the cancellations demoted to a `notice`, so a real break is never buried under the noise this record is about. **IT STILL EXITS 1 ON A CANCELLED RUN, DELIBERATELY** — this job’s name is what branch protection requires (DR-0617: removing the job once left every PR waiting on it forever), so letting a superseded run report success would satisfy the required check with its tests never having run, which is a far worse defect than the one being fixed. **NO GATE MOVED**, proven by table rather than asserted: all-success 0→0, any `failure` 1→1, any `cancelled` with none failed 1→1, any `skipped` 1→1. The real jq programs were dry-run against five `needs` payloads including the actual #2186 one, not reasoned about. Job name and all 14 `needs` unchanged, since a rename here would hang every PR. NOT CLAIMED: that this has run in CI yet — it is a workflow change whose first real exercise is this PR’s own run, and the new wording gets read in anger the first time a run of mine is superseded after it merges. NOT CLAIMED: that cancellation is always supersession — a human cancel and a timeout land in the same bucket, which is why the message says “the usual cause” and tells the reader to check the current head rather than asserting why. NOT ADDRESSED: the concurrency cancellation itself, which is CORRECT and stays — abandoning a superseded run saves real runner time. | [DR-0957](DR-0957-a-tenant-waits-for-the-landlords-yes.md) | **A tenant waits for the landlord’s yes, and the database is what makes them wait.** Darrell 2026-10-11, a fourteen-section directive opening with a claimed leak: “after registering, tenants are being redirected to a page where they can see information that should not be accessible to them”. The test is live and RLS HOLDS; no lease, rent, balance, phone or email reaches a new registrant. What IS real is the SCREEN: the role resolver ends `return ’tenant’`, so a person the system knows nothing about is handed the tenant face — empty, because RLS correctly withheld everything, with no explanation and no way forward. The 2026-08-27 defect wearing the other shoe. An empty screen is not a leak and is still wrong. Now (database half): tenant_portal_requests holds the asking and no access; my_portal_status() is parameterless + SECURITY DEFINER so it can only describe its caller; the grant that opens a door is still rental_tenancies.tenant_user_id and decide_portal_request() is the only thing that writes it; approval LINKS rather than creates, and revoke clears that one column leaving lease, rent and payments untouched; the dropdown includes OCCUPIED doors (the people it exists for live in them) and carries no name, contact or balance; a match is a hint for the landlord and the registrant is never told, since “we found your record” is a way to probe who lives where. THREE DEFECTS FOUND BY ATTACKING MY OWN CODE: (1) a NULL-role authorization hole — user_role_in_instance() is NULL for a non-member, so `IF NOT (NULL IN (...))` NEVER FIRES and a stranger was waved through; only a downstream “seat is taken” check stopped her, which is luck, not a wall; every plpgsql guard is now `IF NOT coalesce(..., false)`; (2) the match was DEAD — email_norm/phone_norm are GENERATED and Postgres computes those AFTER BEFORE-triggers, so it matched nothing while failing nowhere; (3) the smoke proved nothing on its first run — a DO block runs as the session role and postgres BYPASSES RLS, so “a stranger” read 3 tenancies. AND A FALSE CLAIM IN MY OWN MIGRATION IS CORRECTED IN IT: column grants are not a wall here — 0024 sets ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES granting authenticated table-wide DML, so the table was born writable before a GRANT was read; the RLS policies and the trigger are what hold, and they were proven by trying to break them. Applied twice, idempotent; smoke proves 8 behaviours and 11 walls; three breaks each caught. NOT BUILT: the app half — waiting screen, pending role state, registration form, landlord queue, invitations (should reuse property_access_invites from 0150) and notifications; branch not pushed. | [DR-0962](DR-0962-the-stamp-is-asked-of-git-so-a-lane-can-ship-from-its-own-worktree.md) | **The stamp is asked of git, so a lane can ship from its own worktree.** Found shipping DR-0961 from an isolated worktree -- the lane shape ORCHESTRATION section 2 prescribes: `push-stranding-guard: COULD NOT STAMP -- EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '/tmp/wt-pics/.git'`. Proven-to-catch -- and the FIRST attempt was not: it asserted only against the repo the suite runs in, where both paths coincide, so the broken line passed all 14 tests; the test now creates a real worktree and fails with 'the resolved gitdir is not a directory'. | [DR-0764](DR-0764-next-goes-to-the-next-paragraph-and-one-reading-owns-the-voice.md) | **Next goes to the next paragraph, Back to the one before, and one reading owns the voice.** Darrell 2026-10-06, from his phone, a lesson in the NAS voice with all 169 pieces on the device: *"The reader does not go to the next section or paragraph... it goes to the beginning of the lessons"* and *"it gets garbled words at times even with the storage increase for cache."* Measured: `paragraphStarts` grouped sentences by a tag whitelist (P/LI/H1-6/BLOCKQUOTE/TD/TH/DT/DD/FIGCAPTION/PRE) that `buildFollowMap`'s own block list exceeds by twenty tags, so a DIV-rendered lesson resolved every sentence to the one `<li>` wrapping it -- `starts` = `[0]`, Forward `null`, Back segment 0, the top of the lesson. The place was `base + local` with `local` read from whichever counter the mode pointed at, so the jump after a jump used the old run's position (Back after Next went FORWARD). And a read is async for seconds before it plays; a second read inside that window found no queue to stop, so both drove the ONE shared `<audio>` element and the superseded one put its piece on it mid-sentence -- a fully saved reading makes that window LONGER. Fixed: `buildFollowMap` records the block grid and paragraphs are read from it (positions, not live nodes, so a re-render cannot break them); one run-local position put back to 0 whenever a jump sets a new base; every read takes a number and a superseded read installs no queue, touches no element, and never reaches the phone's own voice. Ruled out by measurement: piece length (154,630 pieces, longest 181, none over 200) and index shift (segmentText is prefix-stable; clip keys are content-addressed). 6 assertions proven-to-catch. |

| [DR-0767](DR-0767-the-lesson-body-read-survives-a-long-spoken-word.md) | **The lesson body read survives a long spoken word.** Darrell spoke two teachings into the app 2026-10-06; Whisper wrote the first as `79c29dc9` (`lesson-name:Christyn's Homework`), the NAS builder handed it back failed, and `inbox-lesson-body.yml` then died with no reason: `printf: write error: Broken pipe`, exit 1, none of its three `::error::` messages fired (run 37542689782). Short teachings always worked; long ones died silently. The query now asks for single-line base64 and the step parses with bash string operations, never `head`, taking fields from the end so a `|` in a lesson name cannot shift them; a failed round-trip prints both md5s and the base64 length. Corrected same day: it is a RACE, not a 64 KiB threshold, and Darrell's real row was NOT reproduced here (rebuilt to its exact 34,530-byte/430-line shape the old code exits 0 twelve times of twelve). The kill path is established from the run's own log and demonstrated on a 204,000-byte row that exits 141; the proof that matters is the real re-read on main (run 37544218320), round-trip ok, 24,467 bytes, md5 matching. The builder's own `cli-local structure failed` verdict is named, not guessed at, `re-review: 2026-10-08`. |

| [DR-0801](DR-0801-every-voice-keeps-its-own-pitch-so-one-voice-is-several-readers.md) | **Every voice keeps its own pitch, so one voice is several readers.** Darrell on the Firestick: "Can we choose different male and female voices... different pitches... to get a unique voice that has the right sound for each individual?" and "I only see one option other than my own that doesn't work yet until the 4070 does something." He is right: the picker offers the System voice, consented person voices, and whatever `speechSynthesis.getVoices()` reports on THAT device - a TV browser reports almost none. The Web Speech API has NO gender field, so male and female come only from the voices a device offers; that is recorded here rather than implied. Pitch is the lever we own: the engine has applied one to every utterance since it was written and the Scripture cast already tells characters apart with it, but `useTts` never exposed `setPitch`, so the saved pitch could not change. Now five named steps (Deepest, Deeper, Natural, Lighter, Highest) kept PER VOICE in `voice-shape.js`, all five in the tall panel and one cycling button in the TV rail (DR-0800). One engine voice at five pitches is five readers, with no studio and no 4070. Proven to catch: the pitch measured landing on a real utterance against a fake synth; a non-number never reaching it; rubbish, an array, a bad pitch and a throwing storage all survived - and it caught a real bug on its first run, Number(null) being 0, which would have clamped a missing pitch to the deepest voice there is. |

| [DR-0834](DR-0834-the-storm-you-can-see-coming-and-the-court-where-a-life-hangs.md) | **The storm you can see coming, and the court where a life hangs: what a warning asks of you (L223).** Darrell forwarded NPR's morning newsletter into the app 2026-10-08 with one word on top, Lesson (thread 1a11be8ea0e58748). One subject line carried a hurricane bearing down on the Gulf and a judge ordering execution evidence preserved. They are ONE lesson because they ask one question: somebody was told ahead of time, so what gets done before it is too late? The provenance and its LIMITS are in the lesson, not only in this record: both items are that letter's report on that morning, a forecast is a forecast, what the storm did was NOT checked from this machine and is not claimed, and the court item is kept to exactly what the headline said. The lesson recounts no crime, names no detail of one, and takes no position on any person's guilt, because what is taught is the STANDARD and a standard is never helped by particulars. Three tests enforce that rather than trusting it to care. The storm half: His way is in the whirlwind and He will not acquit the wicked, in ONE verse (Nahum 1:3); He stills it and is the shelter (Psalms 107:28-29; Mark 4:37-39; Psalms 46:1-2; Isaiah 25:4); and He still expects a man to MOVE, which is not in tension with that (Proverbs 22:3 and 27:12, where the simple are never called wicked, only unguarded, and are punished anyway); Noah did ALL of it, said twice (Genesis 6:22; 7:5); and the same storm hits two houses in word-for-word identical weather, so only the foundation differs (Matthew 7:24-27). The court half, taught in THREE parts because all three are written (DR-0098): it AUTHORIZES the magistrate (Genesis 9:6, whose reason is that man is made in His image; Romans 13:3-4); it sets an evidentiary bar almost nobody has read, in the SAME verse that authorizes the penalty (Numbers 35:30; Deuteronomy 17:6; 19:15), with diligent inquisition and the false witness receiving the penalty his lie aimed at (Deuteronomy 19:17-19); and it states HIS OWN HEART twice in the first person (Ezekiel 18:23, 18:32; John 8:7). A lesson carrying only the first reads as appetite, only the second as evasion, only the third as misrepresentation, so every band carries all three and a test requires it. Proverbs 17:15 closes the usual argument: BOTH errors get the same word, so preserving evidence is not a loophole for the guilty but the only way the standard can be met in either direction. Lands on Micah 6:8. Measured: adult 1,268 prose words; child 0.521 / youth 0.604 / teen 0.789 / senior 0.946 of it; FK 2.86 / 5.21 / 6.21 / 7.13 under a 5.0 child ceiling; 16 sections; all 42 anchors taught. Proven-to-catch, seven defects: three movement markers followed a bare (reference) with no period so the reader found 13 sections not 16; hasAllThreeEverywhere was false in four places because "search" is not a verb the friend detector knows; the child band sat at 0.495, a hair under its floor; two spans were quoted with NO reference ("innocent blood" used as a phrase, and a Nahum clause in a facilitator note); Nahum 1:3 was not verbatim because I capitalized a clause that follows a colon and reads lowercase; Genesis 9:6 was not verbatim in four places (a curly apostrophe in man’s typed straight); and two Ezekiel quotes were spliced with an ellipsis, which cost exactly the "saith the Lord GOD" that makes those verses first-person. 24 cases green. `re-review: 2026-11-09` — confirm a reader in a hard season does not feel lectured by the storm half, and that no part of the court half reads as appetite rather than as the standard. |

| [DR-0870](DR-0870-an-empty-unit-is-still-a-place-work-and-people-before-a-tenant.md) | **An empty unit is still a place: work orders and people before there is a tenant.** Darrell 2026-10-10, on the Work Board of 805 North Prospect Avenue Apt 2 with "Add a microwave and cabinet with exhaust fan inside the kitchen." typed in and FILE IT dead: "Workorders don't work... can't send...!?!!!!!" ROOT CAUSE, one line: tenant_maintenance_requests.tenancy_id is uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES rental_tenancies(id) (0055:135), and every write control keys off activeDoor, which IS a tenancy. A vacant property has none, so activeDoor was null and FOUR surfaces died silently at once -- File it disabled, Write the invitation disabled (his earlier screenshot, same cause), sendMessage returned, addNote returned -- and not one of them said why. The premise under the schema is wrong and is named plainly: it encodes that work only happens where a tenant already lives, when fixing up an empty unit before anyone moves in is the most ordinary landlord job there is. Fixing the schema means reworking RLS on five tables that all scope by tenancy_id, so the call is deliberately made app-side where rental_tenancies ALREADY allows it: every tenant column nullable, 'pending' a legal status. A unit with no tenant is a tenancy row with no tenant in it; ensureDoor() makes one on demand and SAYS it did; when someone moves in that same row is filled, not replaced, so the empty unit's work history stays attached to the place it happened. Also fixed, never reported because the first bug hid it: activeDoor fell back to doors[0], so picking a tenancy-less property while holding tenancies elsewhere silently selected a DIFFERENT property's door and would have filed work against the wrong place. 108 properties cases green. Live RLS insert NOT yet proven from the sandbox -- verify on the deployed build. re-review 2026-10-17. | accepted | B | product | REALITY-TRACE, SURFACE-PREMISE-CONFLICTS, DR-0061, DR-0076, DR-0219 |

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: `setBookings` was called from exactly ONE place — the realtime subscription. Every staff control wrote to the database and then WAITED FOR A postgres_changes EVENT to come back and tell it what it had just done; the checkbox is fully controlled by booking.responsibilities, so until that event arrives the tick cannot move, and the write's result was discarded. With the app reaching the NAS cross-origin over the Funnel because every Pages Function is dark (#2057), a long-lived WebSocket is exactly what is most likely not running: the write lands, the screen never moves, the tick springs back, nothing is said. AND UNDERNEATH IT, THE QUIETEST FAILURE IN THE APP: a PostgREST update whose row is filtered out by RLS returns NO ERROR AND ZERO ROWS, so updateBooking returned { ok: true } whether it had saved or done nothing, and no caller could tell. THE RIGHT PATTERN WAS ALREADY IN THIS FILE — the correspondence thread does `if (res.ok) { ...; await load(); }`. Same file, two write paths, opposite discipline; the third time today the cure sat one call site over (cf. DR-1057). FIXED: writes ask what they did (`.select()`; zero rows = 'refused', never a quiet success), hand the saved row back, the surface applies it directly, the tick is optimistic via the PURE nextResponsibilities — the same function the persisted write uses, so an optimistic tick can never predict something the write would not do — and goes BACK on refusal, with the RLS case named in plain words rather than a generic 'could not save'. Realtime is NOT removed; it stops being the only way this screen learns what this person did. PROVEN TO CATCH BY MUTATION TWICE: removing `.select()` → FAIL; leaving the optimistic tick in place after a refusal → FAIL; both reverted, 15/15 green after each. The four ruled-out causes are pinned against the migration so they stay ruled out — if the wiping trigger ever became BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE it would blank the checklist on every save, a different bug wearing this exact symptom. The optimistic arithmetic is pinned against the readout he photographed (officiant ticked = 1/8; tick setup = 2 of the same 8). HONEST LIMIT: it is NOT proven the WebSocket is down — the sandbox has no route to the Funnel, so that is the best-supported explanation, not a measured fact; the ruled-out list is measured, this is inference. The fix is correct EITHER WAY (`re-review: 2026-10-16` to confirm once #2057 is cured). Any surface whose only setX is a realtime callback has this defect; that sweep is its own change (`re-review: 2026-10-22`). | [DR-1064](DR-1064-the-church-issues-the-statement-and-tells-the-truth-about-what-it-is-worth.md) | **The church issues the statement — and tells the truth about what it is worth.** Darrell, 2026-10-16, with the membership agreement open on *"it holds no giving amount and no giving total"*: **"The church has will need to have recorded records for giving for tax purposes..."**, then **"They will have to accept that we do keep these types of records in the signin for the app when they give something... they can also give anonymous... however we need to know all possible data... make sure people know the tax benefits of their church tithe."** THE GAP IS EXACT — NOT A WRONG PROMISE, A MISSING RECORD. Three giving roads already exist and NOT ONE is the document a member needs at tax time, and the two that come close say so themselves: giving-records.js (the giver's OWN owner-only ledger, Matthew 6:3-4) carries the line *"The church's official contribution statement comes from the church office"*, and giving-reports.js (the office's working record from Cash App history) carries *"a working record for the church office — NOT a church-issued tax statement"*. One points at the office, the other says it is not the office's document, and the document was never built. AND THE PROMISE WAS NOT IN CONFLICT, ONLY AMBIGUOUS: "this record holds no giving amount" is TRUE and must stay true — giving never appears on a member card, so nobody reading the roll can see what anyone gives (Matthew 6:3-4 carried in the schema rather than a policy), and that protection is kept word for word. What it must not be read to mean is "the church keeps no record of your giving", because the church MUST keep one and the member NEEDS it. Changing the sentence is safe because signChurchCovenant stores the attestation text WITH EACH SIGNATURE, so a past signer's record still holds exactly what they read (DR-0356). WHAT THE RULES REQUIRE, STATED PLAINLY (IRS Publication 1771): a donor cannot claim a SINGLE contribution of $250 OR MORE without a CONTEMPORANEOUS WRITTEN ACKNOWLEDGMENT, in hand by the earlier of the date they file or the due date; it must carry the organization's name, the cash amount, a DESCRIPTION BUT NOT A VALUE of any non-cash gift, and either "no goods or services were provided" or a description and good-faith estimate of them; and a QUID PRO QUO payment over $75 needs a disclosure that only the excess over value received is deductible. DECIDED: every Pub 1771 element decided FROM THE DATA rather than pasted onto every copy; A NON-CASH GIFT IS DESCRIBED AND NEVER VALUED (the church pricing a donated piano is the church signing a number it did not verify); money in integer cents throughout; and it REFUSES rather than issuing what it cannot stand behind — on a missing legal name or address, an unnamed member, a bad year, or an empty year, because A STATEMENT READING $0 READS LIKE A DENIAL — while a missing EIN WARNS and does not block, since Pub 1771 does not require it but every preparer asks. ANONYMOUS GIVING IS KEPT AND WHAT IT COSTS IS SAID BEFORE THE CHOICE: both halves of his sentence hold and do not fight — the church records every gift AND a giver may keep their name off theirs; an acknowledgment must name the donor, so an anonymous gift cannot be substantiated, stated up front rather than discovered in January, and a year of ONLY anonymous gifts says exactly that instead of "no gifts are recorded", which would be a lie to someone who gave all year. THE TEACHING IS WHERE IT WOULD BE EASY TO DO HARM BY BEING ENCOURAGING: the flat sentence a congregation usually hears — "your tithe is a tax deduction" — IS FALSE FOR MOST HOUSEHOLDS, and the ones it is least true for can least absorb the surprise. So the fact is stated plainly (DR-0100 tier 1: deductible ONLY IF YOU ITEMIZE, and since 2018 most households take the standard deduction and the tithe changes their bill by nothing); what is genuinely open is flagged NARROWLY (tier 2: the figures move every year and the non-itemizer rules have changed more than once) — so NO DOLLAR FIGURE FOR THE STANDARD DEDUCTION IS PRINTED ANYWHERE, because a number typed from memory would be read off a church surface by a family making a real decision and a stale one is worse than none; the teaching carries the TEST and names who holds the current figure (`re-review: 2027-01-15`). The one figure that does not move IS named: the $250 rule. AND THE ORDER, which only this platform will say — the deduction is real AND IT IS SECOND: "Take heed that ye do not your alms before men" (Matthew 6:1, KJV) and "God loveth a cheerful giver" (2 Corinthians 9:7, KJV), both quoted verbatim; nobody tithes for the write-off, knowing what the law allows is stewardship and making it the reason is something else — both said, in that order, neither debated (DR-0098). 33 cases weighted at the ways a statement can HARM the person holding it, a different list from the ways it can be untidy: THE OVER-CLAIM IS PINNED AS A TEST rather than left to good intentions (an assertion fails if a standard-deduction dollar figure is ever printed), an anonymous gift is asserted never to reach a total on a document that names a donor, 300 gifts of $33.33 total exactly $9,999.00, the $250 boundary asserted INCLUSIVE and the $75 boundary EXCLUSIVE with the arithmetic still honest below it. ONE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS WAS WRONG AND THE TEST SAID SO: the rewrite turned "never sold, never sent to..." into "NONE OF IT is ever sold, ever sent to...", whose antecedent is now BOTH records — a real strengthening; the assertion was written against the old wording, and a second case now pins that every refusal sits INSIDE the "none of it" clause so a later tidy-up cannot narrow it back to the member card alone. Every original protection is pinned individually, because the easiest way to do harm here is to lose one while adding a sentence. NOTHING IS WIRED INTO A SURFACE AND NOTHING IS ISSUED: this is the pure core and its proof; the office's issue-and-send control, the stored anonymous flag on a gift row, and the church's legal name / address / EIN fields are a SCHEMA CHANGE AND A TIER-C SEND belonging in their own record with the Governor's hand on them (`re-review: 2026-10-20`).
